result:
I’d make everyone experience, once and unmistakably, the inner life of someone they consider an enemy.

Not to force agreement, forgiveness, or goodness. People would remain free to disagree—even profoundly. But they would know, viscerally, that the other person has fear, memory, private tenderness, and a story in which their own actions make sense.

So much cruelty depends on distance: people becoming categories, numbers, obstacles. I’d collapse that distance for a moment. Not because understanding solves everything, but because afterward, treating someone as disposable would require a much more deliberate lie.
